newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: SOCCER-TRAGEDY-MARKED GUATEMALA STADIUM MAY REOPEN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TRAGEDY-MARKED GUATEMALA STADIUM MAY REOPEN.

text.p: Guatemalan sports promoters said they expected FIFA, World Cup soccer's governing body, to authorise this week the reopening of the Mateo Flores stadium, closed since 78 people died in a tragic crush in October.
Sports authorities here hoped to use the stadium April 16-27 for a Central American soccer cup, the fourth annual "Copa de Naciones."
The disaster at the stadium occurred Oct. 16, half an hour before the kickoff at a World Cup classifying match between Costa Rica and Guatemala.
Overcrowding in the stadium triggered a human avalanche in the cement bleachers where seats were cheapest.
After the tragedy, FIFA suspended all national and international soccer matches in the stadium until significant changes were made to guarantee security for fans.
The Guatemalan Football Federation said on Wednesday it has made all the recommended improvements, and some extra ones.
Authorities said an 800-strong security force, including members of the National Police and private police will guarantee crowd safety at the games.
Investigations by the public prosecutor's office show 60,000 people, including 45,000 ticket holders, unticketed children, and gate crashers, were packed into the stadium on the night of the tragedy.
A group of Guatemalan engineers later said the stadium should hold only 32,676. FIFA has recommended a maximum capacity of 29,934.
